title: MD Forecast Performance Overview
conclusion: Independent confirmation finds small measurable point-error gains for contact count and retained-contact fraction, but no model meets all frozen practical-usefulness criteria (at least 10% gain against both references plus useful uncertainty). Fine-tuning exists and is compared on identical windows. Native fine-tuned MAE at C40/H10 is 11.47 contact pairs, 0.0562 retained fraction (5.62 percentage points), and 0.0816 Å. Contact/fraction intervals under-cover; external fine-tuning worsens minimum-distance error and produces seven crossed contact quantiles. Median curves remain almost flat. Native zero-shot contacts meet the original, smaller measurable-skill minimum; the stricter follow-up criterion remains unmet. This supports limited forecast-level skill and further controlled research, not replacement of MD or practical deployment; it does not prove these predictions are intrinsically impossible.
